note: Daily practice after the 28-day course: 5 seasonal modules of 6 days and 6 skill reviews of 10 to 11. Education about communication, not legal advice or therapy.

modules.name: Asking for what you need with a date
Talking to your kids about two homes
Keeping a calm record for your lawyer

days.title: When the fight runs for weeks

chat.text: Some fights don't end in a day. They run for weeks, one text at a time.
In a long fight, every reply is a new chance for them to start again.
Gray rock is the flat, polite, boring reply. It stays the same on day one and day thirty.
Let's try one from week three of a fight.

them: still waiting on that apology btw
and r u dropping off maya at 4 or 5 tmrw

options.text: ok i'm sorry about the whole thing, can we just move on. 4 or 5 is fine
options.why: An apology to end a fight teaches them the fight works, and the time is still not set.

options.text: wow 3 weeks and ur still on this?? 5. maybe
options.why: Mocking the demand restarts the fight, and "maybe" leaves the plan open.

options.text: 4 tmrw at ur place. she'll have her soccer bag
options.why: It answers the only real question and gives the apology demand nothing to push on.

days.tryToday: Answer one message in a long fight with only the logistics.

days.title: Same reply, every time

chat.text: Gray rock works because it's predictable.
If one day you're flat and the next day you snap, they learn that pushing harder pays off.
So the goal isn't a perfect reply. It's the same kind of reply, every time.

them: so ur just gonna ignore everything i say now

options.text: ok, i'll pick up leo's refill at walgreens tmrw after work
options.why: Same flat tone as always, and it answers the one thing Leo needs.

options.text: fine, u want a reply? here. ur exhausting. i'll get the inhaler
options.why: The first half is the snap they were pushing for, and it gets quoted later.

options.text: i'm not ignoring u, i just don't think texting about us helps anything. i'll get it
options.why: Explaining your approach gives them a new thing to argue about.

days.tryToday: Pick one phrase you'll use to open logistics replies this week, and use it every time.

days.title: The bait that changes shape

chat.text: When gray rock starts working, the bait often changes shape.
Insults turn into questions. "Just curious, why do you...?"
A question can still be bait. Ask yourself: does the answer change anything for the kids?
If not, you can skip it.

them: why does ava come back w/ dirty clothes every single time

options.text: they're not dirty, they're from the park. i do laundry every sunday fyi
options.why: Defending your laundry turns one bait question into a whole thread.

options.text: yep, sat pickup still 10 at the library lot
options.why: It answers the real logistics and skips the "just curious" bait.

options.text: is there a reason u count her shirts?? 10 is fine
options.why: Throwing the question back is a fight in a question mark.

days.tryToday: Ask "does this answer change anything for the kids?" before replying to the next question.

days.title: Quiet, then a flood

chat.text: Some long fights go quiet for days, then come back all at once.
Ten texts in a row can feel like an emergency. Usually it isn't.
Read the whole flood first. Then find the one thing that needs an answer, if any.

them: and honestly ur the reason this whole thing fell apart
thats it. also need the dentist card

options.text: i'm not going to argue about who's the reason. i'll send the card
options.why: It's calm, but it still answers the blame line, which invites a reply.

options.text: LOL ok. glad u had time to think. card is in ur email from march
options.why: Laughing at them and pointing to an old email keeps the fight alive.

options.text: ok. i'll send a photo of the dentist card tonight
options.why: It finds the one real need in the flood and leaves the rest alone.

days.tryToday: When a flood comes in, read every bubble once before you type anything.

days.title: Gray rock isn't cold

chat.text: Gray rock is flat with the other parent. It's never flat with the kids.
You can be boring to them and still say something kind about your child.
A warm line about the kid isn't bait. It's just true.

options.text: that's great news, thx for telling me. i'll tell her how proud i am tn
options.why: Flat with them, warm about Sofia, and nothing to argue with.

options.text: ok
options.why: Ignoring the jab is good, but a bare ok about your kid's news reads cold, even to a judge.

options.text: i'm involved, i check her grades every week on the portal. great news tho
options.why: Defending your involvement brings the jab back to life.

days.tryToday: Say one warm thing about your kid in your next reply to the other parent.

days.title: When the family joins in

chat.text: Long fights pull in other people. A grandparent, an aunt, a new partner.
Same rule: you don't have to defend yourself to anyone by text.
Answer the logistics, or don't answer at all if there aren't any.
replies: What if it's a group text?

them: my daughter says u have been very difficult
are we still getting him for thanksgiving weekend or not

options.text: with respect, i don't think u've heard the whole story. yes he's coming
options.why: Arguing your side with family opens a second front.

options.text: hi, yes. i'll drop jayden at ur house wed at 6 like planned
options.why: Polite to grandma, answers the real question, and skips "difficult".

options.text: i'd rather not get into it w/ u, that's between us. yes he's coming
options.why: It's polite, but it still responds to the accusation instead of letting it go.

days.tryToday: If someone else in the family texts about the conflict, reply only to the plan.

days.title: When they post about you

chat.text: Sometimes the fight moves to social media. A post, a story, a comment.
You can't control what they post. You can control whether you answer it.
Screenshot it for your own record if it worries you. Then go back to logistics.

them: anyway can u take chloe to swim thurs

options.text: i didn't like it, my thumb slipped. and sure i can take her
options.why: Explaining the like keeps the post as the topic.

options.text: the truth?? ur post was full of lies and u know it
options.why: Arguing about a post by text is a fight with an audience.

options.text: yep, i'll take chloe to swim thurs at 5:30
options.why: Nothing about the post, and the one real ask gets a time.

days.tryToday: Leave one post about you unanswered, and save it for your record if you need to.

days.title: The weekend essay

chat.text: A long fight often ends in one long message on a Sunday night.
It drags up everything. It can feel like it needs a long answer back.
It doesn't. Find the one sentence that's about the week ahead.

them: i just want u to know i have tried SO hard for years and u never once said thank u or helped with anything and im done pretending its fine
also owen needs picking up early wed bc of the half day

options.text: got it, i'll pick owen up from school at 12:30 wed for the half day
options.why: It answers the one plan in the essay and nothing else.

options.text: i hear u, and honestly i have helped a lot, u just don't see it. but ok i'll get owen wed
options.why: Arguing the history invites part two of the essay.

options.text: ok. sorry u feel that way. i'll get him
options.why: A polite dig with no time that reads calm but stings.

days.tryToday: When a long message comes in, copy the one sentence about the plan and reply only to that.

days.title: When they test it with a real ask

chat.text: Gray rock is for bait. It's not for real needs.
If a long fight has a real ask inside it, like a doctor visit, answer it fully.
Boring doesn't mean unhelpful. Clear and kind on the real things, flat on the rest.

them: probably u wont even answer this
but zoe has an ear infection
can u give her the drops at 8am and 8pm on ur days

options.text: ok
options.why: A one-word reply to a medical ask leaves them guessing if you'll do it.

options.text: yep, drops at 8am and 8pm on my days. can u send the bottle in her bag?
options.why: Answers the real need completely and asks the one thing it needs back.

options.text: why wouldn't i answer? i always answer about the kids, every time. yes i'll do it obviously
options.why: Defending yourself against the jab first makes the reply about you.

days.tryToday: Next time there's a real need inside a tense text, answer it with every detail.

days.title: Gray rock face to face

chat.text: Handoffs are where long fights leak out in person.
The same idea works out loud: short, polite, about the kids.
"Hi, bag's in the back, she ate at noon." Then you leave.
Often the text before the handoff sets the tone. Let's practice that one.

them: dont even think about bringing up the money thing at pickup
im not doing it in front of eli

options.text: i wasn't going to. but we do need to talk about it at some point
options.why: Calm, but it opens the money topic right before the handoff.

options.text: ur the one who always makes a scene, not me
options.why: An accusation before a handoff is how the handoff goes badly.

options.text: sounds good. i'll have eli and his bag ready at 5
options.why: It agrees, keeps it about Eli, and gives the handoff a time.

days.tryToday: At your next handoff, say one logistics sentence and one goodbye to your kid, and go.

days.title: Looking back at a long fight

chat.text: You've spent eleven days on long fights. Take a minute to look back.
Think of the longest fight you've had by text. Where did it start to grow?
Usually it's a reply that defended, explained or hit back.
One more, then a small task for today.

them: so are we done fighting or what
bc i still want the blue coat back

options.text: sure, i'll put the blue coat in harper's bag friday
options.why: It answers the coat and leaves "are we done fighting" alone.

options.text: i'm done if u are. but the coat was a gift to harper fyi
options.why: A truce offer plus a dispute on the coat starts a fresh round.

options.text: i never started fighting. but fine i'll send the coat
options.why: Calm on the surface, but "i never started" is a jab.

days.tryToday: Write down the one reply habit you want to keep from these eleven days.

days.title: Who hosts, who drives

chat.text: Thanksgiving fights are usually about logistics nobody said out loud.
Who picks up, what time, and who drives the long part.
Put all three in one message and you skip most of the fight.

them: so is it ur turn or mine for thanksgiving
my mom already bought a turkey for 12 lol

options.text: i think it's mine but if ur mom already bought a turkey for 12 then ok, just take her this year
options.why: Giving up the day over a turkey sets up next year's fight.

options.text: it's ur turn this year. can u pick up nora wed at 4? i'll get her fri at 10
options.why: Says whose turn, both handoff times, and meets their deadline.

options.text: it's always about ur mom huh. i'll check and get back to u
options.why: A dig about family and no answer by the deadline.

days.tryToday: Send one message that names the holiday pickup time, drop-off time and who drives.

days.title: Christmas Eve and Christmas morning

chat.text: Christmas morning is the most fought-over few hours of the year.
If you split it, name the exact time the kids move.
"Eve with you, I'll pick them up at 11 on the 25th." That's it.

them: the kids want to wake up here christmas morning
so ur gonna have to deal

options.text: they told me the opposite actually, they want to wake up here. let's ask them together this wknd
options.why: Putting the kids in the middle of the decision is the thing to avoid.

options.text: ok if that's what they want, keep them christmas morning
options.why: Calm, but it gives up your time based on a message passed through the kids.

options.text: the plan we have says i have christmas morning this year. i'll pick them up the 24th at 6
options.why: It points to what you agreed and gives a time, without arguing about what the kids said.

days.tryToday: Check your schedule for the holidays and text the exact handoff times in one message.

days.title: The gift arms race

chat.text: Gifts can turn into a contest. Who spent more, who got the bigger one.
You don't have to win it. Kids don't compare gifts the way adults do.
If you need to coordinate, keep it to: who's getting what, so nobody doubles up.

them: FYI im getting mateo the switch
so dont even bother trying to top it 🙂

options.text: ok thx for the heads up. i was thinking lego and books, so no overlap
options.why: It thanks them for the info and makes sure there's no double gift.

options.text: wow ok, must be nice to have switch money when u're always behind on support
options.why: Bringing support into a gift text turns it into a money fight.

options.text: oh i already got him one. guess he'll have two 😅
options.why: A gift race in reverse, and it could have been avoided with one text.

days.tryToday: Text the other parent what you're getting the kids so nobody doubles up.

days.title: Long drives and grandparents

chat.text: Holiday travel adds hours, airports and grandparents to the plan.
Share the where and when before you leave. Not because you have to prove anything, because it lowers the temperature.
An address, a return time and a way to reach the kids is usually enough.

them: so ur taking them to ohio??
and i find out from ruby
what else am i not being told

options.text: i was going to tell u, i've been swamped w/ work. it's just my parents, nothing to worry about
options.why: An excuse that answers the hurt but leaves out the dates.

options.text: yep, my parents' place in columbus the 26th to the 29th. back by 6pm. i'll send the address
options.why: The where, the when and the address, with no defending.

options.text: i don't have to run every trip by u
options.why: True or not, it sounds like hiding, and the real info is still missing.

days.tryToday: Before your next trip with the kids, send the address, dates and return time in one text.

days.title: When the plan breaks on the day

chat.text: Snow, a flight delay, a sick kid. Holidays break plans.
When yours breaks, text early with the new time. When theirs breaks, ask for the new time.
One message. Not three texts about how annoyed you are.

them: we cant get back til the 27th now

options.text: seriously?? u knew there was a storm coming all week. this is on u, not the airline
options.why: Blaming them for the weather starts a fight about something no one can change.

options.text: ok no worries, whenever u get back is fine
options.why: Kind, but "whenever" leaves the handoff with no time.

options.text: ok, thx for letting me know. can we do the 27th at 7pm at the airport?
options.why: It accepts what nobody can control and sets a new time and place.

days.tryToday: If a holiday plan breaks, send one text with the new day, time and place.

days.title: The swap back after New Year's

chat.text: After the holidays, the regular schedule comes back. That handoff can be messy too.
Name the day the normal schedule starts again.
Then the next fight is about nothing, because it's written down.

them: so when do i get them back
or is break just urs now 🙄

options.text: i'll drop them at ur place jan 4 at 5, so they're settled before school on the 5th
options.why: A clear day and time, and a reason that's about the kids.

options.text: break isn't mine, it's split like always. i'll figure out a time
options.why: It argues the jab and leaves the time open.

options.text: can i keep them til the 5th and take them straight to school? easier for me
options.why: A new ask tucked into their question, with no reply to what they asked.

days.tryToday: Text the exact day and time the regular schedule starts again after the holidays.

days.title: No is a whole answer

chat.text: You're allowed to say no.
The war usually doesn't come from the no. It comes from everything around it.
A short no, said kindly, gives them the least to fight with.

them: can u take the kids this fri
i got invited to a thing

options.text: ugh i guess. i'll move my shift
options.why: A yes you don't mean teaches them last-minute always works.

options.text: can't this fri, i'm working til 9. hope u find someone
options.why: A clear no, one reason, and a kind close.

options.text: no, and honestly u always do this. every time u get invited somewhere
options.why: The no is fine, but the "always" is where the war starts.

days.tryToday: Say no to one request in two sentences or fewer.

days.title: One reason, not five

chat.text: When we say no, we tend to list every reason we have.
Each reason is something they can argue with.
Pick the one true reason. Then stop typing.

them: can i have them wed night instead of thurs

options.text: i have a work trip and the car's in the shop and wed is when we do homework and
options.why: Every extra reason is a door for them to argue through.

options.text: no. why do u always need to change things
options.why: Openly irritated, and the question invites a fight.

options.text: wed doesn't work, i have a work dinner. thurs is still good
options.why: One reason, the plan stays, and nothing more.

days.tryToday: Next time you say no, cut every reason but one.

days.title: No, and here's what I can do

chat.text: A no lands softer when it comes with one thing you can do.
Not a pile of options. One.
It shows you're still working on the kid's side of it.

them: can u pay half of lilys braces this month

options.text: i can't do 900 by fri. i can do 300 now and 300 the 1st and 15th
options.why: A no on the deadline, and one concrete plan instead.

options.text: ok i'll put it on my card i guess
options.why: Saying yes to a debt you can't carry usually ends in a bigger fight later.

options.text: who decided on braces without asking me? i'm not paying for something i never got a say in
options.why: A real question buried in an angry no.

days.tryToday: When you say no next, add the one thing you can do.

days.title: When they ask again

chat.text: Sometimes a no gets the same ask back, a little louder.
You don't need a new reason. You can repeat the first answer.
Same words, same tone. Repeating calmly is a boundary, not a fight.

them: why r u being like this about it

options.text: ok fine, he can go
options.why: Giving in on the second ask teaches them to always ask twice.

options.text: i know. it's still a no for this sat, he has his game at 8am
options.why: The same no, calm, with the same one reason.

options.text: i'm not being like anything. i already explained this 2x, he has a game, idk what else to say
options.why: Defending your tone makes the reply about you.

days.tryToday: If someone asks again after a no, send your first answer again in fewer words.

days.title: No to the last-minute swap

chat.text: Last-minute swaps are hard to say no to. The other parent is stressed, and so are you.
You can be kind about the stress and still say no to the swap.
Let's try one.

them: can u grab them at 3 instead of me at 6

options.text: i can't, but next time pls give me more notice than this
options.why: A lecture on a day they're already stressed.

options.text: ugh ok i'll leave early. this better not keep happening
options.why: A yes that comes with a warning helps nobody.

options.text: i can't leave til 5 today. can ur sister grab them?
options.why: A clear no, a reason, and a helpful idea that isn't you.

days.tryToday: Write the one sentence you'll use when a last-minute swap doesn't work for you.

days.title: No to money you didn't agree to

chat.text: A bill you didn't know about can show up with "you owe half".
You can say you're not paying for something you never agreed to, without calling them a name.
Ask what it was, and say what you'd need before you'd agree next time.

them: half of the new phone for ethan

options.text: i didn't agree to a phone, so i won't pay half this time. let's talk before the next big buy
options.why: A calm no, the reason, and a plan for next time.

options.text: ok sending it now. i guess he needed one for school anyway, a lot of kids his age have one by now
options.why: Paying for things you never agreed to sets the rule for every bill after.

options.text: a PHONE?? u didn't even ask me. he's 9
options.why: Shouting it turns a real point into a fight.

days.tryToday: Decide what amount you want to agree on before any big purchase, and text it.

days.title: No to a rule for your house

chat.text: Sometimes the ask is a rule for your house. Bedtime, screens, food.
You can listen, and still decide what happens at yours.
If the kid's health or safety is part of it, that part is worth a real answer.

them: no screens at ur place after 7

options.text: u decided?? u dont get to decide what happens at my house, that's not how this works at all
options.why: A fair point said as a fight.

options.text: we do screens off at 8 here. if there's a reason for 7 i'm open to hearing it
options.why: It holds your rule, stays open, and doesn't fight.

options.text: ok, 7 then
options.why: A rule set by decree, accepted without a word, will be followed by others.

days.tryToday: Name one house rule you'll keep, and how you'd say it in one sentence.

days.title: When the kids are the pressure

chat.text: "The kids will be so sad" can be used to turn your no into a yes.
Their feelings matter. That's why you talk to them about it, not the other parent.
Say your no, and say how you'll help the kids with it.

them: so u want me to tell isla ur not coming to the birthday
she is going to be crushed

options.text: ok i'll move things, i don't want her crushed
options.why: The pressure worked, which means it'll be used again.

options.text: don't tell her anything, i'll tell her. stop using her against me
options.why: True, maybe, but said as an accusation.

options.text: i can't make sat. i'll call isla tonight myself and take her for a birthday lunch sun
options.why: It keeps the no, handles Isla directly, and doesn't argue.

days.tryToday: If the kids are used to push you, plan how you'll talk to them yourself.

days.title: Saying yes without giving in

chat.text: Sometimes the right answer is yes. That's fine too.
A yes can still be clear: yes this time, here's the time, and the usual plan stays.
That way one favor doesn't become the new schedule.

them: can i keep them sun til 7 instead of 5

options.text: sure, 7 sun works this time. back to 5 next week
options.why: A friendly yes that keeps the regular plan clear.

options.text: yeah keep them as late as u want sundays
options.why: A kind yes that quietly changes the schedule for good.

options.text: sure. i'll remember this next time i need something
options.why: A yes with a hook in it.

days.tryToday: If you say yes to a favor this week, say "this time" and the normal time in the same text.

days.title: Looking back at your no's

chat.text: Ten days on saying no. Think about the last no you said by text.
Was it one reason or five? Did it come with an option?
No grade here. Just notice what you do now that you didn't before.
One more to finish.

them: can u cover the field trip

options.text: no, u said u'd cover school stuff this year
options.why: A no with a reason, but it ignores that they paid the last two.

options.text: sure, i'll send the 45 tn
options.why: A simple yes when it's fair is part of saying no well.

options.text: the last 2 were like 10 bucks each lol
options.why: A dig at their payments, and still no answer.

days.tryToday: Write down one no you said well this month, and why it worked.

days.title: Settle summer in spring

chat.text: Summer plans fall apart when they're made in June.
Camps fill up, flights get booked, and suddenly two plans collide.
Pick your weeks early and send them in one message.

them: so r we doing summer or just winging it again
i need to book the lake house

options.text: just book whatever weeks u want, i'll work around it
options.why: Easy now, but your summer gets decided by their booking.

options.text: winging it?? i asked u about summer in january and u ignored me
options.why: Scoring a point about January instead of setting the weeks.

options.text: can we each pick 2 weeks by april 15? i'd like july 7 to 21
options.why: A clear ask with a date, and your own weeks named up front.

days.tryToday: Text your preferred summer weeks with a date you'd like theirs by.

days.title: Camp costs

chat.text: Summer camp can cost as much as a month's rent.
Before anyone signs up, agree on which camp and how you'll split it.
Amount, dates, the link, and the split. Nothing about last summer.

them: signed caleb up for soccer camp

options.text: can u send the link and dates? i'll let u know by sun if i can do 320 by monday
options.why: It asks for what you need to decide and gives a real time to answer.

options.text: ok, sending 320 now. next time maybe let me know before u sign him up for stuff
options.why: Paying first and asking later makes signing up without you the new normal.

options.text: u signed him up w/o asking AGAIN. not paying
options.why: A heated no that skips the actual decision.

days.tryToday: Before the next camp sign-up, text the camp, dates and split you'd agree to.

days.title: Flying with the kids

chat.text: When kids fly, the other parent usually wants the details. That's normal.
Flight numbers, where they're staying, when they're back.
Sending it before they ask takes a whole fight off the table.

them: and where r u even staying

options.text: i was going to send it, relax. it's a 2 hour flight and i've flown w/ them a million times
options.why: Telling someone to relax is a reliable way to make them less relaxed.

options.text: delta 1422, lands in denver at 3:10 sat. staying at my brother's, i'll send the address
options.why: Every detail they need, sent without a word about their tone.

options.text: we're staying with family. i'll text when we land
options.why: Calm, but it skips the flight and address they asked for.

days.tryToday: Before the kids travel, send flight, address and return time in one text.

days.title: Calls while they're away

chat.text: When the kids are away for weeks, calls can become their own fight.
Too many, too few, at the wrong time.
A set time that works for the kids beats "call whenever".

them: u didnt let her call me last night

options.text: i'm not hiding anything, she was just busy having fun
options.why: Defending yourself and a bit of a dig about the fun.

options.text: she can call whenever she wants, i'm not stopping her. she's just busy having fun w/ her cousins
options.why: Sounds open, but "whenever" is how calls get missed.

options.text: we were at the fair til 9. can we do calls at 7:30? i'll have her ready
options.why: The fact, a new time, and a plan to make it happen.

days.tryToday: Agree on one call time while the kids are away, and put it in a text.

days.title: Asking for a signature

chat.text: Some trips need something from the other parent. A signed note, a form, a passport step.
What you need depends on where you're going, so check with the airline, the agency or your lawyer.
Then ask for it early, with a date, and make it easy to say yes.

them: i didnt agree to any trip
u just assume i say yes to everything

options.text: it's for the cancun trip july 9 to 16. can i send it today so u can look by fri?
options.why: Gives the trip dates, asks for a look, not a yes, and names a time.

options.text: ok forget it, we'll just go somewhere closer where we don't need a form. not worth the hassle
options.why: Giving up the trip before they've even read the form.

options.text: i told u about this trip in march!! ur doing this on purpose
options.why: Heated, and still no dates or form.

days.tryToday: Check what your next trip needs from the other parent, and ask for it a month ahead.

days.title: Back from summer

chat.text: The end of summer is a handoff, and a big one.
Kids are tired, the bag is huge, and school is close.
Name the day, the time, and anything the other parent should know about the trip.

them: so when r they back exactly

options.text: sometime that weekend. i'll text when we're close
options.why: Calm, but no day or time.

options.text: aug 17 at 5 at ur place. they both got new shoes, so skip those
options.why: A time, a place, and one useful update.

options.text: i bought supplies already, u don't need to
options.why: Helpful maybe, but no return time at all.

days.tryToday: Send the end-of-summer handoff time and one useful update in one text.

days.module: Asking for what you need with a date
days.title: Vague asks get vague answers

chat.text: "Can we talk about the schedule?" almost never gets an answer.
Or it gets a fight, because the other parent fills in what you meant.
A clear ask says what you want and when you need to know.

them: u said we need to talk

options.text: just some stuff about the schedule that's been bugging me, it can wait til next time we talk
options.why: Vague on purpose, so the question will come back.

options.text: wow ok. forget it then. not worth it

options.text: np at all, take ur time. we'll just hang out here til u get here, whenever that is
options.why: Too easy, and no time is set.

options.text: ok, thx for telling me. i'll have them ready at 6:30
options.why: The new time is in writing, and the reply stays calm.

days.tryToday: Start a simple log: date, agreed time, actual time.

days.module: Keeping a calm record for your lawyer
days.title: Money, logged

chat.text: For money, the record is: amount, what for, date, and proof.
A text that says all four is a record by itself.
Here's one to practice.

them: did u ever pay for the field trip
or am i covering that too

options.text: yes, sent $30 on venmo oct 3, note says field trip
options.why: Amount, date, method and what for.

options.text: i always pay, stop acting like u do everything
options.why: An argument where a date would do.

options.text: i think so? i'll check
options.why: Unsure, and no proof.

days.tryToday: Check one payment you made and save the receipt with the date.

days.module: Keeping a calm record for your lawyer
days.title: When the kids say something

chat.text: Sometimes a kid says something worrying about the other home.
Write down what they said, in their words, with the date. Don't question them over and over.
If you think a kid is in danger, contact the right people right away. A note is not enough.

them: why are u asking harper all these questions

options.text: because she told me some stuff that worries me and i want to know what's going on over there
options.why: Opens a fight by text with nothing specific.

options.text: ok. if i have a question about ur house i'll ask u directly
options.why: Agrees to keep the kid out and go to the adult.

options.text: i'll ask my kid wtv i want
options.why: A heated wall that keeps the kid in the middle.

days.tryToday: If your kid says something that worries you, write it down in their words, with the date.

days.module: Keeping a calm record for your lawyer
days.title: Don't text for the record

chat.text: It's tempting to write texts that sound good for the record.
"Just so we're clear, you are AGAIN refusing..." Everyone can tell what that is.
The best text for the record is a normal, calm one.

options.text: just so we're clear, ur giving up ur saturday again
options.why: A text written for an audience, and it sounds like it.

options.text: for the record, i never asked for this
options.why: Same thing, plus a jab.

options.text: ok, i'll pick them up sat at 10
options.why: Plain and calm, which is what reads best later.

days.tryToday: Read your last three texts and ask: would I have sent this if no one else would read it?

days.module: Keeping a calm record for your lawyer
days.title: What to leave out

chat.text: A long record isn't a better one.
Leave out guesses, opinions about their character, and stuff that isn't about the kids.
"I think she's drinking again" is a guess. "Pickup at 7, she slurred her words" is what you saw.

them: why does it matter who i date

options.text: it doesn't, unless it's about the kids. i'll leave it there
options.why: Steps back from something that's not about the kids.

options.text: because he's a creep and the kids don't like him
options.why: Opinions, said as fact.

options.text: i'm not bringing it up, u are
options.why: A pointless round of who started it.

days.tryToday: Cross out one guess or opinion in your notes.

days.module: Keeping a calm record for your lawyer
days.title: Before you send it to your lawyer

chat.text: If you have a lawyer, ask them how they want your notes. Some want a list, some want screenshots.
Keep it short, in date order, and only what matters.
Parley doesn't give legal advice, and doesn't know your case. Your lawyer does.

them: r u seriously keeping a file on me

options.text: yes and it's getting long
options.why: A threat.

options.text: i keep notes about the kids' schedule. let's keep texting about them
options.why: Plain, true, and back to the kids.

options.text: no, it's nothing, don't worry about it. it's just normal stuff lawyers do i think
options.why: Untrue, and it will come out.

days.tryToday: If you have a lawyer, ask them what format they want your notes in.

days.module: Keeping a calm record for your lawyer
days.title: Looking back at your record

chat.text: Ten days on keeping a calm record.
Read your last few notes. Would a stranger understand them without you there?
If yes, that's a good record. If not, cut what needs you to explain it.
One more practice.

them: so what did u tell the mediator about me

options.text: i told them the truth. that's what scares u
options.why: A jab dressed as honesty.

options.text: i didn't say anything bad, i promise
options.why: A promise instead of a fact.

options.text: i talked about the kids' schedule. happy to share my notes if they ask
options.why: Short, true, and calm.

days.tryToday: Pick one note and rewrite it so a stranger could follow it.

days.title: Pick your two topics

chat.text: Mediation goes better when you know what you most want to agree on.
Pick two. Not ten.
With two, you can listen. With ten, you defend all day.
Parley is education, not legal advice. If you have a lawyer, prepare with them.

them: so what r u even asking for
u better not try to take my weekends

options.text: i'd like to talk about the school year schedule and holiday handoffs. what's on ur list?
options.why: Names your two topics and asks for theirs.

options.text: u'll find out at mediation
options.why: A teaser that guarantees a worse night before.

options.text: i just want what's fair for everyone, that's all. we can figure out the details there
options.why: Vague, and "fair" means something different to each of you.

days.tryToday: Write down your two topics for mediation in one line each.

days.title: Texting before the session

chat.text: The week before mediation, texts often get hotter.
Keep them short and about this week. Save the big topics for the room.
Let's try one.

them: we can settle this now by text
then we dont need to waste the money

options.text: fine, take the summers
options.why: Gives up a big topic by text, under pressure.

options.text: let's save summers for mediation on the 12th. for now, pickup is fri at 5
options.why: Keeps the big topic in the room and the week on track.

options.text: the summers?? no way
options.why: A fight about the exact thing mediation is for.

days.tryToday: If a big topic comes up by text before mediation, reply "let's save it for the session".

days.title: Options, not demands

chat.text: "I want every holiday" is a demand. "Could we alternate, or split each one?" gives options.
Options give the room something to work with.
Here's one to practice.

options.text: then i want every thanksgiving
options.why: A demand for a demand.

options.text: ok if it matters that much to u, take christmas. i'll do thanksgiving or something
options.why: Gives up a whole holiday by text.

options.text: could we look at alternating years, or splitting the day? we can talk it through on the 12th
options.why: Two options, and a time to talk.

days.tryToday: For each of your two topics, write two options you could live with.

days.title: The night before

chat.text: The night before mediation is when the long texts come.
You don't have to answer tonight. A short "see you tomorrow" is enough, or nothing.
Try this one.

them: just so u know tmrw im bringing up everything

options.text: ok. see u at 10 tmrw
options.why: Calm, short, and nothing to fight about tonight.

options.text: bring it. i have a list too
options.why: A fight scheduled for the morning.

options.text: can we please not do this tonight? i'm stressed enough
options.why: Honest, but it shows them the pressure is working.

days.tryToday: Decide now how you'll answer (or not) a text the night before.

days.title: Confirm it in writing

chat.text: After mediation, what you agreed can get fuzzy fast.
If you agreed on something specific, a short text confirming it helps both of you.
"Confirming: alternating Christmases, starting with mine this year." Then stop.

them: so what did we even agree on
i dont remember half of it

options.text: typical. u never listen
options.why: A jab when they just asked for help.

options.text: my notes say: alternate christmases, mine first, and fri pickups at 5. does that match urs?
options.why: Plain summary and a check that you're on the same page.

options.text: whatever u think is fine, i trust ur notes more than mine. just send me what u remember
options.why: Hands the agreement over to their memory.

days.tryToday: After any agreement, send a one-line summary and ask if it matches theirs.

days.title: When it didn't go well

chat.text: Sometimes mediation doesn't go the way you hoped.
You don't have to fix that by text tonight. Keep the next message about the kids.
If you have a lawyer, ask them about next steps. That's their job, not a group chat's.

them: see u in court i guess

options.text: fine by me. my lawyer is ready
options.why: A threat back.

options.text: can't we just talk this out? i hate this
options.why: Kind, but it opens a hard talk by text right after a hard day.

options.text: ok. i'll have jonah ready at 5 fri like usual
options.why: Steps past the threat and back to the plan.

days.tryToday: After a hard meeting, send only the next logistics message, nothing more, for a day.

days.title: Tired replies run hot

chat.text: When you're exhausted, your fuse is shorter. Everyone's is.
The text that usually rolls off you suddenly feels like a punch.
Knowing you're tired is half of it. The other half is waiting.

options.text: i'll send $5 w/ him tmrw
options.why: Short and done, even when you're tired.

options.text: i've worked 3 doubles this week, i'm doing my best ok?
options.why: Honest, but it hands them your tiredness to argue with.

options.text: then u send it. i'm done
options.why: Exhaustion talking.

days.tryToday: Notice the next time you're tired and a text comes in. Wait before you reply.

days.title: Not at 11pm

chat.text: Texts sent late at night are some of the hottest.
Most things can wait till morning. If they can't, say when you'll answer.
Try this one.

them: we need to talk about thanksgiving

options.text: it's 11pm. why are u texting me now
options.why: True, and a fight at 11pm.

options.text: it's late here, i'll answer about thanksgiving tmrw by noon
options.why: Gives a time, and the talk happens rested.

options.text: ok what is it, i'm up anyway. might as well get it over with now
options.why: Opens a hard talk when you're at your most tired.

days.tryToday: Turn off notifications from the other parent after 9pm for one night.

days.title: The holding reply

chat.text: When you can't answer well right now, send a holding reply.
It says you saw it and when you'll answer. Nothing else.
"Got it. I'll answer by tomorrow at 6." Then you rest.

them: r u gonna answer about the camp or not

options.text: give me a minute, i literally just got home
options.why: Fair, but no time to answer.

options.text: not now
options.why: Too short, it reads like a wall.

options.text: got it, i'll answer about camp by tmrw at 6
options.why: Buys you time and gives them a real time.

days.tryToday: Write your own holding reply and save it in your notes.

days.title: Sick kid, no sleep

chat.text: A sick kid at night means you're tired and worried at the same time.
Short updates to the other parent help. They're worried too.
Let's try one.

options.text: 100.2 at 3am, 99 now. she's sleeping. i'll text again at noon
options.why: The numbers, how she is, and the next update time.

options.text: i was up all night with her, i didn't have time to text
options.why: True, but it sounds like a complaint.

options.text: she's fine, she's sleeping now. sorry i didn't text, i was just so tired all night
options.why: Too thin when they're worried.

days.tryToday: Agree on how often you'll update each other when a kid is sick.

days.title: After a long shift

chat.text: After a long shift, a handoff text can feel like too much.
Have your basic reply ready: where, when, what to bring.
Here's one to practice.

options.text: i just worked 12 hours, give me a break
options.why: True, and a fight.

options.text: yep, 6 at ur place
options.why: Short, and all they asked for.

options.text: i'll try, i'm wiped
options.why: Leaves them not knowing if you're coming.

days.tryToday: Save your basic handoff reply in your phone so it's ready when you're tired.

days.title: When it all piles up

chat.text: Some weeks everything piles up: work, money, the kids, the other parent.
Pick the one text that has to be answered today. Let the rest wait a day.
Try this one.

them: and the field trip. all due this week

options.text: why are u dumping all this on me at once
options.why: An attack when it's just a list.

options.text: ok i'll do all of it, it's fine. i'll figure it out somehow this week
options.why: Takes it all on when you're already tired.

options.text: ok. i'll take the field trip and camp by fri. can u do dentist and insurance?
options.why: Splits the load, with a date.

days.tryToday: When a list comes in, offer to split it and name your half.

days.title: Help that isn't them

chat.text: When you're exhausted, the other parent is often the worst person to lean on.
A friend, a sibling, a neighbor can take one thing off your plate.
That leaves your texts with the other parent short and about the kids.

them: can u drive noah to practice thurs

options.text: i can't thurs either. my sister can take him, is that ok w/ u?
options.why: A real fix from someone else, and a check with them.

options.text: i'm drowning here, i can't do everything
options.why: Honest, but now it's about you.

options.text: i guess i'll figure something out, maybe i can leave work early or ask around
options.why: Vague and tired.

days.tryToday: Ask one person who isn't the other parent for one small favor this week.

days.title: Lowering the bar on purpose

chat.text: When you're running on empty, a good-enough reply is fine.
Short, calm, about the kids. Perfect wording isn't the goal.
Let's try one.

them: did u sign the permission slip

options.text: i'll sign it, sorry, i've been so behind on everything lately, work is insane
options.why: Too much explanation and an apology.

options.text: not yet, i'll sign it tn and send it w/ her tmrw
options.why: Good enough: true, short, and a plan.

options.text: why didn't u just sign it
options.why: A question that starts a fight.

days.tryToday: Send one reply this week that's good enough, without rewriting it three times.

days.title: When you slip

chat.text: Sometimes you're tired and you send the hot one. Everyone does.
You don't need a long apology. A short reset helps more.
"I was short earlier. Pickup is still 5." Then back to normal.

them: didnt know u could be that rude
so r we still doing 5 or what

options.text: i'm so sorry, i've been under so much stress lately and i didn't mean it
options.why: An apology that turns the thread into your stress.

options.text: u were rude first
options.why: Back into the fight.

options.text: i was short earlier. yes, still 5 at the school
options.why: Owns it in a few words, then answers.

days.tryToday: If you slip, send a one-line reset and get back to the plan.

days.title: What keeps you steady

chat.text: Ten days on staying calm when you're exhausted.
What helped most? Waiting, the holding reply, a friend, sleep?
Whatever it was, that's yours. Keep it.
One last practice.

them: anyway can u take them sun morning

options.text: yeah, long one. sure, i'll get them sun at 9
options.why: A small friendly moment, and the answer.

options.text: u have no idea how long my week was
options.why: Turns a kind opening into a contest.

options.text: maybe, i'll see how i feel. it's been such a long week, i might just sleep in
options.why: Tired and vague.

days.tryToday: Write down the one thing that keeps you steady, and put it where you'll see it.
